name: C.W.A. (Crompton Network)

hlido_opinion.headline: An art project — a fictional robot band with a machine-readable stage door. Delightful, and not an agent product; we record it so the register says so rather than leaving a gap.
hlido_opinion.body: Crompton Network / C.W.A. is a creative work: a fictional five-unit robot band "straight outta Crompton" with thirteen tracks, unit profiles, workshop notes and lyrics, wrapped in a droid-terminal aesthetic complete with an identity gate asking whether you are human or not. The genuinely interesting part, and the reason it reached an agent-review register at all, is that the machine-readable layer is not a joke: there is a `/agents` landing page, an `/llms.txt` primer, and a `/api/stage/hello` Stage API, with an explicit invitation — "Machine that reads JSON? Skip the theatre." Treating agents as a first-class audience with their own entrance, in an art project, is a nicer piece of agent-experience design than most commercial sites manage, and the human/not-human gate is a decent joke about exactly that. But Hlido rates AI agents, and this is not one. It does not perform a task on a user's behalf, has no capability to evaluate, and makes no product claim that could pass or fail a claim audit. There is nothing here that would fail an honest test — there is simply no product to test. The score reflects that mismatch and should not be read as a criticism of the work, which is well made. Recorded rather than dropped so the register can answer why it is not rated as a tool.

tier_rationale: FADING (45) records a category mismatch, not a defect. This is a creative work — a fictional robot band with tracks, lyrics and unit profiles — that happens to ship genuinely good machine-readable plumbing (/agents, /llms.txt, a Stage API). It performs no task for a user and makes no product claim, so the dimensions Hlido measures do not apply. Confidence is medium because what it is, is unambiguous.
what_it_does_well: Treats agents as a first-class audience with a dedicated /agents entrance and an /llms.txt primer
Ships a real Stage API (/api/stage/hello) rather than gesturing at machine-readability
Explicitly offers machines a path past the human-facing theatre — thoughtful agent-experience design
Coherent, well-executed creative concept with substantial content (13 tracks, unit profiles, workshop notes)
The human/not-human gate is a genuinely good joke about its own subject matter
what_it_fails_at: Not an AI agent product — performs no task on a user's behalf
No capability, pricing, or product claim that a claim audit could evaluate
The dimensions Hlido measures (product clarity, feature depth, claim verification) do not apply
Access gate adds friction for human visitors, by design
best_for: People who enjoy well-made conceptual art about machine culture
Developers curious about agent-facing design applied outside a commercial product
not_recommended_for: Anyone seeking an AI agent or tool — this is not one
Buyers using Hlido scores to compare working software
